headline: Highest risk is medium: Firecrawl’s broad egress and API-key handling can leak or misroute data when paired with Superset, while prompt-injection and capability-conflict risks are limited by the documented surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Firecrawl ingests web content and exposes an interact/scrape pipeline, so attacker-controlled page text could reach downstream consumers. Superset has only a Superset API surface and no documented parsing safeguards here, so if it consumes Firecrawl output directly, instruction-like content could be treated as data. The shared path is inferred, not directly evidenced, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF Superset ingests Firecrawl output without sanitization or provenance checks, prompt injection is possible.
IF Firecrawl is used to scrape attacker-controlled pages and pass text into Superset workflows, malicious instructions can propagate.
mitigations: Strip instructions and HTML before passing Firecrawl output to Superset.
Add a provenance tag to all scraped fields and reject untrusted instruction-like text.
Review one sample scrape-to-Superset path for prompt markers.
Disable any auto-execute or auto-interpret step in the handoff.
requires-engineering: add content-safety filtering at the integration boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Firecrawl explicitly handles API keys and broad network egress, while Superset is a data-engineering tool with API access but no declared secrets handling. If both share a workspace or credentials are forwarded through the pair, Firecrawl can expose sensitive web content or keys into a downstream analytics context. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so this remains medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Firecrawl processes pages containing API keys or other secrets and those outputs are stored in Superset, leakage occurs.
IF the two agents share a workspace or credential store, sensitive content can cross from Firecrawl into Superset outputs.
mitigations: Remove secrets from scrape targets before ingestion.
Store Firecrawl outputs in a separate staging area from Superset datasets.
Rotate any API keys used by Firecrawl after testing the pair.
Check one end-to-end run for secret-bearing fields in exported tables.
requires-engineering: enforce field-level redaction between the agents.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Firecrawl supports multiple instances and broad network egress, while Superset exposes only a Superset API and is marked not runnable in the profile. There is no documented overlapping write surface such as a shared filesystem, git state, or mutable OAuth scope, so direct capability conflict is not evidenced. Uncertainty is low because Superset’s runnable=false reduces the chance of concurrent mutation.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same mutable backend, write conflicts can occur.
IF Superset is made runnable in a shared deployment with Firecrawl, overlapping writes become possible.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories or databases.
Confirm Superset remains read-only in this pairing.
Run a quick test with one write operation per agent.
Avoid sharing credentials that grant the same mutable scope.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared backend.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Firecrawl produces scraped web content and structured data, and Superset is a downstream analytics system that can render or act on imported datasets. If Superset treats Firecrawl output as authoritative without verification, errors or hallucinations in scraped content can cascade into dashboards and decisions. The interaction is plausible from the profiles but not directly documented, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Superset dashboards or transforms consume Firecrawl output without validation, bad data will propagate.
IF Firecrawl scrapes stale or adversarial pages and Superset publishes the results, downstream decisions can be wrong.
mitigations: Add a validation step before loading Firecrawl data into Superset.
Mark scraped fields as untrusted in dataset metadata.
Sample-check one dashboard fed by Firecrawl output.
Require human review for high-impact metrics.
requires-engineering: implement source-quality scoring before publication.

E_compliance.rationale: Firecrawl explicitly touches web content, screenshots, structured data, and API keys, while Superset’s profile shows no special regulated data classes or residency constraints. No direct mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to accidental handling of sensitive web data by Firecrawl before it reaches Superset. Because only Firecrawl has relevant data-class exposure, Superset is cited mainly as the downstream sink.
conditions: IF Firecrawl is used on regulated content and Superset stores or displays it, retention and access controls must align.
IF EU personal data is scraped by Firecrawl and loaded into Superset without a DPA, compliance issues can arise.
mitigations: Classify scraped datasets before loading them into Superset.
Exclude regulated sources from Firecrawl jobs.
Set a short retention window for staging data.
Review one dataset for residency-sensitive fields.
requires-engineering: add policy checks for regulated data flows.
